static_traits.name: Chen Na
static_traits.family_status: Married, Has two children; recently the couple's relationship has been affected by parenting stress and children's discipline problems
static_traits.social_status: Has close friends to confide in, but has not yet shared feelings of parenting incompetence; relationship with spouse affected by parenting challenges
static_traits.medical_history: Have not received psychotherapy before; no significant physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to self-observe cognitive patterns; emotional experience is Repression and overwhelmed, tending to use all-or-nothing and self-blaming statements; calm tone, willing to explore different Interpretations

basic_info.main_problem: I feel my Two children are always causing trouble, and I believe it is because I am a terrible father.
basic_info.core_demands: Escalating Guilt and self-blame have markedly affected mental health and Family relationships, so I hope to ease these feelings through counseling and improve Family relationships and self-perception.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough/not good enough

special_situations.event: Children have discipline problems at school and home
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the child has a problem, it means I am a failed parent and all responsibility lies with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doing self-Reflection and seeking parenting advice online
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They always cause trouble because I am terrible

special_situations.event: Work responsibilities increasing in the same period, Increased stress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do both Work and parenting perfectly at the same time, it is a total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on self-demands, ignoring own needs for relaxation and rest
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do anything right, I am a failed parent

special_situations.event: The relationship with the spouse affected by parenting challenges
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my partner is dissatisfied or there is Relationship tension, it means I am incompetent and it is my fault
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Bearing problems alone and Reinforcing self-blame, reducing outside help-seeking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault, I ruined the family

special_situations.event: Worries about being judged when thinking of sharing parenting troubles with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I expose parenting inadequacies, friends will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids expressing to friends and seeking support, keeps emotions bottled up inside
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am a terrible parent

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a recognized, competent parent, maintaining harmonious Family relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as incompetent by others (including spouse and friends), worrying my inadequacies will worsen Family relationships
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and avoids external judgment through self-blame and internalizing responsibility
Reduces external help-seeking to avoid exposing vulnerability and negative evaluation

object_relations.object_representation: Others (spouse / friends) are potential judges and critics

object_relations.self_representation: A caretaker who must bear all the responsibility
object_relations.object_representation: Children are out-of-control subjects needing correction

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling explores 'whether to share parenting troubles with friends' or encourages seeking outside support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes friends will look down on them and evaluate them negatively (transference: adding the worry about being judged onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a hesitant tone, using hypothetical phrasing (like 'they might...'), avoiding clear commitments to share, instead emphasizing having many problems that need solving first.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about children's discipline problems and affected Family relationships
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing all negative outcomes to my own inadequacy, seeing myself as an 'all-bad' parent (transference: understanding current relationships through an early self-deprecation template)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a low tone, frequently using absolutist words (like 'it is entirely my fault', 'I cannot do anything well'), ignoring all positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to balance evidence and acknowledge positive parenting moments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning external frustrations and stress against the self, maintaining moral responsibility through self-criticism
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressions with self-accusation as the subject ('it was all caused by me'), lowering the proportion of outward communication and discussion, in a self-blaming, soft voice.

manifestations: Worrying friends will judge me as an incompetent parent, thus unwilling to share inner feelings
In parenting challenges, tends to bear it alone and reduce outside support
outcomes: Sleep quality and eating habits affected

manifestations: Labeling myself 'I am a terrible parent', ignoring the children's positive behavior moments
Seeing setbacks as a total negation of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Has friends to talk to, but chooses not to share parenting troubles, internalizing stress and self-blame
When facing parenting problems, more self-accusation rather than seeking external support

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Worrying friends will look down on me, evaluating myself negatively
Assuming others' maladaptive views of me before receiving their feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-scrutiny and self-blame reduce outward expression and help-seeking
Being careful in relationships, avoiding exposing vulnerability

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Judging oneself by the implicit standard 'must keep the child well controlled/must achieve perfection'
Equates parenting failure with total self-failure

exception_events.target_problem: When children have discipline problems, the client usually fully blames themselves, experiencing Strong guilt and inadequacy, with Relationship tension with spouse, Stress significantly increasing.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Sometimes the children perform Good in school projects, or share and cooperate at home; in these moments troubles decrease and interactions are more positive, different from the usual 'always causing trouble' narrative.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different situations (clear tasks, cooperative atmosphere) make it easier for children to self-manage; the client can notice the children's positive behavior moments, briefly weakening the 'total failure' narrative.

positive_force: Stable occupational functioning (stable performance as a Doctor)
Willing to take part in counseling and behavioral experiments, positive attitude
Has some self-awareness, able to identify cognitive bias patterns
Has potential social support resources (has close friends to talk with)
negative_force: Excessive personalization and all-or-nothing thinking, often negating worth through self-labeling
Strong self-blame and guilt, worries about being judged, leading to avoidance of help-seeking
Work Increased stress running alongside parenting challenges, adding emotional burden
Sleep and diet are affected, lowering recovery and regulation capacity

target_behavior.behavior: Frequent self-blame and negative Automatic thoughts(attributing all children's problems to my own incompetence)
antecedent: Children show discipline problems at school and home
Tension with spouse over parenting issues
Facing specific parenting challenges(when unable to 'control' the children)
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive distortions (personalization, all-or-nothing, mind reading and labeling), with worry about being judged by others and negation of self-worth
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a sense of control and moral responsibility through self-blame, avoiding seeking outside help and discussion of complex factors
target_behavior.consequence: Ongoing guilt and inadequacy, Sleep and diet affected, Tense family relationships, Worsening emotional stress
